working: Reflexive: a divides a for every natural a. Transitive: a|b and b|c imply a|c. Not symmetric: 2|4 but 4 does not divide 2, which also rules out 'equivalence relation'. So reflexive and transitive only.
Positive terms 1 + 27 + 125 + 343 + 729 = 1225; negative terms 8 + 64 + 216 + 512 = 800. 1225 - 800 = 425. (Equivalently the sum telescopes as 1 + sum over k of ((2k+1)^3 - (2k)^3).)

Put x = a-b, y = b-c, z = c-a, so x + y + z = 0 identically. The hypothesis is 2y^2 = x^2 + z^2. From x + z = -y we get x^2 + z^2 = y^2 - 2xz, so 2y^2 = y^2 - 2xz, i.e. y^2 = -2xz, i.e. 2/y = -(y)/(xz) = (x+z)/(xz) = 1/x + 1/z. That is exactly the condition for 1/x, 1/y, 1/z to be in AP, and the step is reversible. Verified numerically with y = 1, x = -(1+sqrt3)/2, z = (sqrt3-1)/2: squares 1.866, 1, 0.134 are in AP and reciprocals -0.732, 1, 2.732 are in AP.

(x-a)(x-b) = c is x^2 - (a+b)x + (ab-c) = 0, so alpha + beta = a+b and alpha*beta = ab-c. Then (x-alpha)(x-beta) + c = x^2 - (a+b)x + (ab-c) + c = x^2 - (a+b)x + ab = (x-a)(x-b), whose roots are a and b.

Let the roots be r and r^2. Product r^3 = 3/3 = 1. r = 1 gives sum 2 = -p/3, i.e. p = -6, inadmissible since p > 0. The other cube roots of unity give roots omega and omega^2 with sum -1 = -p/3, so p = 3. Check: 3x^2 + 3x + 3 = 0 has roots omega, omega^2 and (omega)^2 = omega^2, so one root is indeed the square of the other.

The product ends in 1, 3, 7 or 9 exactly when it is odd and not divisible by 5, which forces every factor's last digit into {1,3,7,9} (any factor ending in an even digit makes the product even; any ending in 5 makes it end in 5 or 0). Each factor's last digit is one of 10 equally likely digits, so the probability is (4/10)^4 = (2/5)^4 = 16/625. Verified by enumerating all 10^4 last-digit combinations: 256/10000 = 16/625.

Setting that equal to -2 and clearing the denominator cancels the -2x^2 and -2y^2 terms on both sides and leaves x + 2y - 2 = 0, a straight line (strictly, the line minus the point (0,1) where the denominator vanishes -- that point does lie on the line).
notes: The stem prints the denominator's z carrying a DOT accent (pandoc 'overset dot over z'), which is not standard notation in a complex-locus problem -- a dot over z is a time derivative, meaningless here. I read it as plain z, the standard anthologised form of this problem, which yields the straight line x + 2y - 2 = 0. If instead the dot is a mangled CONJUGATE bar, i.e. Im((2z+1)/(i*conj(z)+1)) = -2, the same rationalisation gives -x + 4y^2 + 6y + 2 = 0, i.e. x = 4y^2 + 6y + 2, a PARABOLA -- option C. A determinant equals that of its transpose, so A = |a b c; d e f; l m n|. B = |l m n; a b c; d e f| is that same matrix with its rows cyclically shifted (third row brought to the top), a 3-cycle and therefore an even permutation, so the determinant is unchanged: B = A and A - B = 0. Verified symbolically (A - B expands to 0, while A + B is twice a non-zero general expression, so option A fails).
